Apply Meek's orientation rules

Source: R/cpdag.R
mc_orient_meek.Rd

Orients every edge whose direction is implied by the edges already oriented, by repeated application of Meek's four rules until no further edge can be oriented.

Usage

mc_orient_meek(amat, ambiguous = NULL, required = NULL, forbidden = NULL)

Arguments

amat

a square 0/1 adjacency matrix with zero diagonal, in the package convention: amat[i, j] = amat[j, i] = 1 is an undirected edge \(i - j\), amat[i, j] = 1 with amat[j, i] = 0 is an arc \(i \to j\), and both zero is no edge.

ambiguous

optional integer matrix with three columns \((i, k, j)\), one row per unshielded triple whose center could not be decided. Both orders of the endpoints are treated as the same triple.

required

optional integer matrix with two columns \((from, to)\), arcs the orientation must contain.

forbidden

optional integer matrix with two columns \((from, to)\), arcs the orientation must not contain.

Value

The oriented adjacency matrix, with attributes "meek_conflicts" (edges two rules wanted in opposite directions, left undirected), "meek_iterations", "meek_blocked" (the number of orientations withheld by an ambiguous triple) and "knowledge", a list recording the arcs imposed and whether the result stayed acyclic and kept every required arc.

The four rules

$$\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{R1} & c \to a,\ a - b,\ c\ \mathrm{and}\ b\ \mathrm{nonadjacent} \Rightarrow a \to b\\ \mathrm{R2} & a \to c \to b,\ a - b \Rightarrow a \to b\\ \mathrm{R3} & a - b,\ a - c,\ a - d,\ c \to b,\ d \to b,\ c\ \mathrm{and}\ d\ \mathrm{nonadjacent} \Rightarrow a \to b\\ \mathrm{R4} & a - b,\ a - c,\ a - d,\ c \to d,\ d \to b,\ c\ \mathrm{and}\ b\ \mathrm{nonadjacent} \Rightarrow a \to b \end{array}$$ R1 to R3 are complete when the only oriented edges are those of the v-structures, so the completed partially directed acyclic graph (CPDAG) of a Markov equivalence class needs no more than those three (Meek, 1995). R4 is idle in that case and becomes necessary as soon as edges are oriented from outside, through required or forbidden, because the graph is then no longer the CPDAG of any class and the first three rules stop being complete. For an input that admits a consistent extension, the four together return the maximally oriented partially directed graph: an edge is left undirected exactly when the background knowledge and the v-structures admit an acyclic extension with each of its two directions.

Background knowledge

required lists arcs that must be present with the stated direction and forbidden arcs that must not. An undirected edge whose reverse is forbidden is oriented, since only one direction is left. Both are applied before propagation and are checked for internal consistency: an arc required in both directions, an arc both required and forbidden, an arc required between responses the skeleton does not join, and an arc required against an edge already oriented the other way are all refused. An incompatibility that only surfaces during propagation, such as a cycle, is reported in the returned attributes rather than raised, because the partially oriented graph is still informative about where the incompatibility lies.

Ambiguous triples

Under the conservative and majority rules an unshielded triple can be left undecided, and propagation must not settle by implication what the separations left open. R1, R3 and R4 all orient an edge in order to avoid creating a collider at its tail, so each is withheld when the triple carrying that collider is ambiguous. R2 only forbids a cycle and involves no unshielded triple, so it is applied unconditionally. Leaving ambiguous at NULL reproduces the unrestricted rules exactly.

References

Meek, C. (1995). Causal inference and causal explanation with background knowledge. Proceedings of the 11th Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence, 403-410.

Verma, T. and Pearl, J. (1990). Equivalence and synthesis of causal models. Proceedings of the 6th Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence, 220-227.

See also

Other structure discovery: mc_find_vstructures(), mc_ges(), mc_graph_pipeline(), mc_pc_skeleton(), mc_residual_df(), mc_separating_sets(), mc_skeleton_to_bnlearn()

Examples

# 1 -> 3 <- 2 with 3 - 4: R1 orients 3 -> 4
a <- matrix(0L, 4, 4)
a[1, 3] <- a[2, 3] <- 1L
a[3, 4] <- a[4, 3] <- 1L
mc_orient_meek(a)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4]
#> [1,]    0    0    1    0
#> [2,]    0    0    1    0
#> [3,]    0    0    0    1
#> [4,]    0    0    0    0
#> attr(,"meek_conflicts")
#> [1] from to  
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
#> attr(,"meek_iterations")
#> [1] 2
#> attr(,"meek_blocked")
#> [1] 0
#> attr(,"knowledge")
#> attr(,"knowledge")$required
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> 
#> attr(,"knowledge")$forbidden
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> 
#> attr(,"knowledge")$n_imposed
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> attr(,"knowledge")$acyclic
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> attr(,"knowledge")$required_kept
#> [1] TRUE
#> 

# background knowledge on a fully undirected chain 1 - 2 - 3
b <- matrix(0L, 3, 3)
b[1, 2] <- b[2, 1] <- b[2, 3] <- b[3, 2] <- 1L
mc_orient_meek(b, required = rbind(c(1L, 2L)))   # 1 -> 2 forces 2 -> 3
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    0    1    0
#> [2,]    0    0    1
#> [3,]    0    0    0
#> attr(,"meek_conflicts")
#> [1] from to  
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
#> attr(,"meek_iterations")
#> [1] 2
#> attr(,"meek_blocked")
#> [1] 0
#> attr(,"knowledge")
#> attr(,"knowledge")$required
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    1    2
#> 
#> attr(,"knowledge")$forbidden
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> 
#> attr(,"knowledge")$n_imposed
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> attr(,"knowledge")$acyclic
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> attr(,"knowledge")$required_kept
#> [1] TRUE
#>
